title: Judges Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 8.

questions.question: Why did the men of Ephraim chide Gideon sharply?
options: Because he called them last to fight the Midianites
Because he did not call them when he went to fight the Midianites
Because he defeated the Midianites without their help
Because he took all the spoils for himself
questions.correctAnswer: Because he did not call them when he went to fight the Midianites
questions.explanation: The men of Ephraim said unto him, 'Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites?' showing their sharp chiding because he did not call them (Judges 8:1).

questions.question: What metaphor did Gideon use to compare Ephraim's help to his own?
options: The gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim is better than the vintage of Abiezer
The harvest of Ephraim is sweeter than the wine of Abiezer
The wheat of Ephraim is finer than the barley of Abiezer
The oil of Ephraim is purer than the honey of Abiezer
questions.correctAnswer: The gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim is better than the vintage of Abiezer
questions.explanation: Gideon said, 'Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?' to show Ephraim's significant contribution (Judges 8:2).

questions.question: Who did God deliver into the hands of the men of Ephraim?
options: The princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb
The kings of the children of the east
questions.correctAnswer: The princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb
questions.explanation: God delivered into the hands of Ephraim the princes of Midian named Oreb and Zeeb (Judges 8:3).

questions.question: How many men did Gideon have with him when he passed over Jordan pursuing the Midianites?
questions.correctAnswer: Three hundred
questions.explanation: Gideon came to Jordan with the three hundred men that were with him (Judges 8:4).

questions.question: What did Gideon ask the men of Succoth to give to his faint men?
questions.correctAnswer: Loaves of bread
questions.explanation: Gideon requested the men of Succoth to give loaves of bread to the faint men following him (Judges 8:5).

questions.question: How did the princes of Succoth respond to Gideon's request for bread?
options: They gladly gave bread to the men
They questioned if the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna were in Gideon's hand
They sent gifts to Gideon instead
They asked for payment before giving bread
questions.correctAnswer: They questioned if the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna were in Gideon's hand
questions.explanation: The princes of Succoth asked, 'Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army?' (Judges 8:6).

questions.question: What did Gideon threaten to do to the men of Succoth if the LORD delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into his hand?
options: Tear their flesh with thorns and briers
questions.correctAnswer: Tear their flesh with thorns and briers
questions.explanation: Gideon said he would tear the flesh of the men of Succoth with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers (Judges 8:7).

questions.question: How did the men of Penuel respond to Gideon's request as compared to the men of Succoth?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The men of Penuel answered Gideon as the men of Succoth had answered him, refusing his request (Judges 8:8).

questions.question: What did Gideon say he would do to the tower of Penuel when he came again in peace?
questions.correctAnswer: Break it down
questions.explanation: Gideon told the men of Penuel, 'When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower' (Judges 8:9).

questions.question: Approximately how many men were with Zebah and Zalmunna in Karkor?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifteen thousand
questions.explanation: Zebah and Zalmunna had about fifteen thousand men with them at Karkor (Judges 8:10).

questions.question: Where did Gideon go to attack the Midianite host securely encamped?
options: By the way of them that dwelt in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah
questions.correctAnswer: By the way of them that dwelt in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah
questions.explanation: Gideon went up by the way of them that dwelt in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah and smote the host (Judges 8:11).

questions.question: Who did Gideon capture when Zebah and Zalmunna fled?
options: Zebah and Zalmunna, the two kings of Midian
questions.correctAnswer: Zebah and Zalmunna, the two kings of Midian
questions.explanation: Gideon pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, took them, and discomfited all the host (Judges 8:12).

questions.question: True or False: Gideon asked the men of Penuel to give him loaves of bread because his men were pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: It was the men of Succoth, not Penuel, whom Gideon asked for loaves of bread because his men were faint and pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna (Judges 8:5).

questions.question: True or False: The host of Midian was secure when Gideon attacked them by the way of Nobah and Jogbehah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states the host was secure when Gideon smote them (Judges 8:11).

questions.question: In what order did these events happen in Judges 8: Gideon asked for bread from Succoth, Gideon pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, men of Penuel refused Gideon's request, Gideon crossed the Jordan?
options: Gideon crossed Jordan, asked for bread from Succoth, men of Penuel refused, then pursued Zebah and Zalmunna
Gideon asked for bread from Succoth, crossed Jordan, pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, men of Penuel refused
Men of Penuel refused, Gideon crossed Jordan, pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, then asked for bread from Succoth
Gideon pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, crossed Jordan, asked for bread, men of Penuel refused
questions.correctAnswer: Gideon crossed Jordan, asked for bread from Succoth, men of Penuel refused, then pursued Zebah and Zalmunna
questions.explanation: Gideon first crossed Jordan (v4), then asked Succoth for bread (v5), men of Penuel refused similarly (v8), and then Gideon pursued Zebah and Zalmunna (v12).

medium.title: Judges Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Gideon do when he returned from battle before the sun was up?
options: He caught a young man of the men of Succoth and enquired of him
He went to the elders of Penuel
questions.correctAnswer: He caught a young man of the men of Succoth and enquired of him
questions.explanation: Judges 8:13-14 shows that Gideon returned from battle early and captured a young man from Succoth to gain information about the city’s leaders.

questions.question: How many elders did the young man describe to Gideon as leading Succoth?
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy-seven
questions.explanation: Judges 8:14 states there were threescore and seventeen men, which is seventy-seven elders leading Succoth.

questions.question: What was Gideon's response to the men of Succoth who refused to give bread to his weary men?
options: He threatened to tear their flesh with thorns and briers
He forgave them and moved on
questions.correctAnswer: He threatened to tear their flesh with thorns and briers
questions.explanation: Judges 8:15-16 shows Gideon confronted the men of Succoth with Zebah and Zalmunna present, then punished the elders with thorns and briers for refusing aid.

questions.question: What did Gideon do to the city of Penuel when they answered him like the men of Succoth?
options: He beat down the tower and slew the men of the city
He ignored them and went forward
He built a tower for protection
questions.correctAnswer: He beat down the tower and slew the men of the city
questions.explanation: Judges 8:17 recounts Gideon’s destruction of the tower of Penuel and the killing of its men because they refused to help him as Succoth did.

questions.question: According to Judges 8:18, how did Zebah and Zalmunna describe the men they killed at Tabor?
options: As men like Gideon, resembling children of a king
As common soldiers with no honor
questions.correctAnswer: As men like Gideon, resembling children of a king
questions.explanation: Judges 8:18 shows Zebah and Zalmunna admitted the men slain at Tabor were noble and strong, similar in stature to Gideon himself.

questions.question: What did Gideon reveal about the men slain at Tabor in relation to himself?
options: They were his brethren, sons of his mother
questions.correctAnswer: They were his brethren, sons of his mother
questions.explanation: Judges 8:19 states Gideon said the slain men were his brothers, emphasizing his personal grief and the seriousness of the conflict.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Gideon’s firstborn son, Jether, when commanded to slay Zebah and Zalmunna?
options: He did not draw his sword because he was afraid
He asked for help from his father
questions.correctAnswer: He did not draw his sword because he was afraid
questions.explanation: Judges 8:20 explains Jether, being young, was afraid and did not act when instructed to kill the kings.

questions.question: Who ultimately killed Zebah and Zalmunna?
questions.correctAnswer: Gideon
questions.explanation: Judges 8:21 recounts Gideon himself rose and killed the kings after Jether’s refusal, demonstrating his leadership and resolve.

questions.question: What did the men of Israel ask Gideon to do after he delivered them from Midian?
options: Rule over them and his descendants
questions.correctAnswer: Rule over them and his descendants
questions.explanation: Judges 8:22 shows the Israelites requested Gideon to be their ruler along with his son and grandson because of his victory over Midian.

questions.question: How did Gideon respond to the offer to rule over Israel and his descendants?
options: He refused, saying the LORD would rule over them
He asked for time to consider
He said only his son would rule
questions.correctAnswer: He refused, saying the LORD would rule over them
questions.explanation: Judges 8:23 records Gideon’s refusal to become king, emphasizing that God alone should be Israel’s ruler.

questions.question: What did Gideon request from the men of Israel after the battle?
options: Every man’s golden earrings taken from their prey
A portion of the spoils for himself
A permanent army under his command
questions.correctAnswer: Every man’s golden earrings taken from their prey
questions.explanation: Judges 8:24 records Gideon’s request for gold earrings from the Ishmaelites as a symbol of victory and thanksgiving.

questions.question: How does Judges 8:25 show the response of the people to Gideon's request for earrings?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 8:25 states the people willingly gave their earrings, showing their support and gratitude for Gideon's leadership.

questions.question: The golden earrings Gideon collected weighed over a thousand shekels of gold.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 8:26 specifies the weight of golden earrings was 1,700 shekels, indicating a significant amount of wealth collected.

questions.question: Gideon made a golden ephod from the earrings and it led Israel to worship the LORD faithfully.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 8:27 reveals that although Gideon made an ephod, Israel went astray and worshiped it, which became a snare to him and his house.

questions.question: What was the result of Gideon's victory over Midian according to Judges 8:28?
options: The land was quiet for forty years
questions.correctAnswer: The land was quiet for forty years
questions.explanation: Judges 8:28 describes that after Gideon subdued Midian, the land had peace for forty years during his lifetime.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 8.

questions.question: What did the men of Israel willingly give to Gideon as a request after the battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Golden earrings from the prey
questions.explanation: Judges 8:25 states that the men willingly gave the earrings of their prey, which were golden, to Gideon as his request.

questions.question: How much did the golden earrings that Gideon requested weigh?
questions.correctAnswer: One thousand seven hundred shekels
questions.explanation: Judges 8:26 records that the weight of the golden earrings was one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold.

questions.question: What did Gideon make from the gold he collected, which became a snare to him and his house?
questions.correctAnswer: An ephod
questions.explanation: Judges 8:27 explains that Gideon made an ephod from the gold and placed it in Ophrah, which became a snare to him and his house.

questions.question: For how many years was the land at rest during the days of Gideon?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty years
questions.explanation: Judges 8:28 states that the country had peace for forty years during Gideon's lifetime.

questions.question: Where did Jerubbaal, also known as Gideon, dwell after the battles?
questions.correctAnswer: In his own house
questions.explanation: Judges 8:29 notes that Jerubbaal, son of Joash, returned and lived in his own house after the war.

questions.question: How many sons did Gideon have according to Judges 8?
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy
questions.explanation: Judges 8:30 records that Gideon had seventy sons by his many wives.

questions.question: What was the name of the son born to Gideon's concubine in Shechem?
questions.correctAnswer: Abimelech
questions.explanation: Judges 8:31 states that Gideon's concubine bore him a son named Abimelech.

questions.question: How is Gideon's death described in the chapter?
options: He died in a good old age
questions.correctAnswer: He died in a good old age
questions.explanation: Judges 8:32 tells us that Gideon died in a good old age and was buried in his father's sepulchre.

questions.question: What happened to Israel immediately after Gideon's death?
options: They turned again to worship Baalim and made Baalberith their god
They continued to worship the LORD faithfully
They appointed a new judge immediately
They built a memorial for Gideon
questions.correctAnswer: They turned again to worship Baalim and made Baalberith their god
questions.explanation: Judges 8:33 indicates that Israel quickly returned to idolatry, worshipping Baalim and Baalberith after Gideon's death.

questions.question: What did Israel fail to remember after Gideon's death?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 8:34 explicitly states that the children of Israel did not remember the LORD who had delivered them from their enemies.

questions.question: Did Israel show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal after Gideon's death according to Judges 8?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 8:35 states that Israel did not show kindness to Gideon's house despite all the good he had done for them.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of Israel's repeated turning away from God after deliverance found in Judges 8:33-35?
questions.correctAnswer: Judges 2:11-15
questions.explanation: Judges 2:11-15 similarly describes Israel turning away from God after periods of deliverance, paralleling Judges 8:33-35.

questions.question: The term 'ephod' which Gideon made from the gold earrings, is best understood as what in the Hebrew context?
options: A priestly garment or sacred object
questions.correctAnswer: A priestly garment or sacred object
questions.explanation: In Hebrew, 'ephod' refers to a sacred priestly garment or object used in worship, as seen in Judges 8:27 and Exodus 28:6-14.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently seen in Judges 8:33-35, illustrating Israel's cyclical faithfulness and apostasy?
options: Inclusio, framing Israel’s faithfulness and apostasy
Chiasm, reversing the order of events
Metaphor, comparing Israel to a vineyard
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing Israel’s faithfulness and apostasy
questions.explanation: The passage uses inclusio by framing the narrative with Israel’s deliverance and subsequent apostasy, a common Judges theme, seen here in verses 33-35.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God raising deliverers like Gideon to save His people, as seen in Judges 8?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 11:32-34
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:32-34 mentions judges and deliverers like Gideon as examples of faith, connecting with Judges 8’s account of deliverance.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Gideon's response to the men of Ephraim in Judges 8:2-3 teach about humility and God's use of different peoples in His deliverance?
options: That Gideon considered himself superior to Ephraim
That God's deliverance involves different roles and no one should boast
That Ephraim was unimportant in God's plan
That only military might determines God's favor
questions.correctAnswer: That God's deliverance involves different roles and no one should boast
questions.explanation: Judges 8:2-3 shows Gideon humbly acknowledging that Ephraim's role was crucial ('gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer') and that God used various people for deliverance, teaching humility and divine sovereignty. This aligns with teachings in 1 Corinthians 12:14-20 about different members in one body.

questions.question: How does Judges 8:4 depict the perseverance of Gideon and his men, and what theological principle does this illustrate?
options: Perseverance in human strength alone leads to victory
Faithful endurance despite weakness glorifies God’s power
Victory depends on numbers and weapons
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful endurance despite weakness glorifies God’s power
questions.explanation: Judges 8:4 describes Gideon and his 300 men as 'faint, yet pursuing,' illustrating that spiritual perseverance amid weakness evidences God's strength, echoing 2 Corinthians 12:9 about God's power made perfect in weakness.

questions.question: What does the refusal of Succoth and Penuel to provide aid to Gideon in Judges 8:5-8 reveal about human sinfulness and its consequences?
options: Pride and selfishness lead to judgment and retribution
Trusting in human alliances is sufficient
questions.correctAnswer: Pride and selfishness lead to judgment and retribution
questions.explanation: Judges 8:5-8 shows these cities refusing bread out of pride and suspicion, resulting in Gideon's threat of harsh punishment, illustrating sin's consequences and God's justice, consistent with Proverbs 16:18 on pride leading to downfall.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by the subduing of Midian in Judges 8:10-14 despite their large numbers?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence
questions.explanation: Judges 8:10-14 recounts Gideon's victory over a large hostile force, demonstrating God's omnipotence—His unlimited power to deliver His people against overwhelming odds, as also seen in Exodus 14:13-14.

questions.question: How does Gideon's creation of the ephod from the golden earrings in Judges 8:24-27 teach about the dangers of idolatry even among God’s deliverers?
options: Idolatry is only a problem for the unfaithful
Even God’s chosen can fall into sin through misplaced worship
Ephods were always acceptable religious symbols
questions.correctAnswer: Even God’s chosen can fall into sin through misplaced worship
questions.explanation: Judges 8:27 states Israel went 'a whoring after it,' showing that despite Gideon's leadership, the ephod became a snare, illustrating human susceptibility to idolatry. This warns about the subtlety of sin, paralleling warnings in 1 Corinthians 10:12.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine justice is demonstrated by Gideon's punishment of Succoth and Penuel in Judges 8:16-17?
options: God’s justice includes human agents executing judgment
God is indifferent to human sin
Sin does not affect communal relationships
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice includes human agents executing judgment
questions.explanation: Judges 8:16-17 records Gideon executing judgment on those who refused aid, illustrating that God’s justice can be mediated through human instruments, as seen with other judges and prophets (Romans 13:4).

questions.question: How does the conversation between Gideon and Zebah and Zalmunna in Judges 8:18-21 highlight the value of human life and the cost of conflict?
options: It shows that kings were insignificant
It reveals the familial nature of conflict and the tragedy of fratricide
It downplays the loss of life
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the familial nature of conflict and the tragedy of fratricide
questions.explanation: In Judges 8:18-21, the kings acknowledge the slain were like kings' children and Gideon calls them 'brethren,' showing the profound tragedy of human conflict and loss, emphasizing the biblical view of the sacredness of life (Genesis 9:6).

questions.question: What theological principle about leadership is taught by Gideon's refusal to rule over Israel in Judges 8:22-23?
options: Leaders should always seek political power
God alone is the true ruler over His people
Human kingship is the highest authority
questions.correctAnswer: God alone is the true ruler over His people
questions.explanation: Judges 8:22-23 records Gideon's refusal of kingship, asserting 'the LORD shall rule over you,' teaching the doctrine of God's sovereign kingship and rejection of human self-exaltation, consistent with 1 Samuel 8:7.

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined doctrinal insight about God's providence and human responsibility emerges from Judges 8:11 and Judges 8:16-17?
options: God acts alone without human involvement
God's providence works through human obedience and judgment
Human actions are irrelevant to divine plans
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence works through human obedience and judgment
questions.explanation: Judges 8:11 shows Gideon's successful attack due to the enemy’s complacency, while 8:16-17 shows Gideon executing judgment on cities refusing aid, together teaching that God's providence includes human obedience in executing justice, echoing James 2:17.

questions.question: Synthesis: How do Judges 8:28 and Judges 8:34 together illustrate the cycle of Israel's faithfulness and apostasy?
options: Israel remained faithful after Gideon’s death
Deliverance leads to long-lasting peace without relapse
Despite God’s deliverance and peace, Israel quickly returns to idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: Despite God’s deliverance and peace, Israel quickly returns to idolatry
questions.explanation: Judges 8:28 records 40 years of peace after Midian's defeat, but 8:34 shows Israel’s immediate return to Baal worship, revealing the persistent human tendency toward sin despite divine mercy, consistent with Romans 7:15.

questions.question: Synthesis: What does the contrast between Judges 8:23 and Judges 8:33 teach about God's kingship and Israel's rejection of it?
options: Israel always honored God as king
God relinquishes His kingship when rejected
Israel’s rejection of God’s rule leads to spiritual unfaithfulness and idolatry
Human kingship is preferable to divine rule
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s rejection of God’s rule leads to spiritual unfaithfulness and idolatry
questions.explanation: Judges 8:23 affirms God's rule, but 8:33 shows Israel turning to Baalim after Gideon's death, demonstrating the consequence of rejecting divine kingship is spiritual apostasy, aligned with Hosea 13:4.

questions.question: What does Judges 8:29-31 reveal about the human dimension of God's chosen leaders and the potential challenges that arise from their families?
options: The leader’s large family can introduce future complications
questions.correctAnswer: The leader’s large family can introduce future complications
questions.explanation: Verses 8:29-31 note Gideon's many sons and his concubine's son Abimelech, foreshadowing future strife (Judges 9), teaching that human family dynamics can complicate leadership and God's plan, as seen also in 1 Samuel 8:1-3.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most reflected in Judges 8:35 regarding Israel’s lack of gratitude toward Gideon despite his deliverance?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s forbearance and mercy
questions.explanation: Judges 8:35 shows Israel’s ingratitude despite Gideon’s goodness, illustrating God’s patient mercy in enduring human unfaithfulness, consistent with Psalm 103:8.

questions.question: What does the capture and execution of Zebah and Zalmunna in Judges 8:20-21 teach about the seriousness of divine justice and the role of courage in fulfilling God's will?
options: Divine justice requires courage and decisive action
questions.correctAnswer: Divine justice requires courage and decisive action
questions.explanation: Judges 8:20-21 reveals Jether's fear but Gideon's courage to carry out execution, teaching that fulfilling divine justice demands boldness, exemplified also by Joshua in Joshua 1:9.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the violence and harsh punishments in Judges 8 show a capricious God inconsistent with love. What does Judges 8:16-17 and 8:28 actually teach about God's justice and mercy?
options: God’s justice includes righteous judgment to maintain covenant faithfulness, balanced by mercy shown in deliverance and peace
God’s punishments are unrelated to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice includes righteous judgment to maintain covenant faithfulness, balanced by mercy shown in deliverance and peace
questions.explanation: Judges 8:16-17 shows God’s justice enacted through Gideon on unhelpful cities, while 8:28 highlights divine mercy in subduing Midian and granting peace, teaching that God’s justice serves covenant faithfulness, consistent with Nahum 1:3.
